title: How to maintain your privacy online
titleChinese: 如何在网上保护个人隐私？
paragraphs: Some of us like to keep some things private – maybe we don’t want people knowing about our relationship status, our age or where we live – because these details are personal. The problem is, everywhere we go online, we seem to leave a digital footprint.

On our social media accounts, we often display things like our opinions, connections and holiday snaps. The issue is, how do we stop everybody seeing everything? Maybe we don’t want a random stranger knowing our favourite type of coffee. And cookies – there was a time they were just something nice to eat. Now they seem to be popping up on websites. So how can you stay more private?

There are some steps you can take. First, on your social media accounts, check your privacy settings. Many social media platforms allow everything to be visible by default, and the onus is on you to set your boundaries. And limiting the amount you share isn’t only confined to social media. There are many sites out there that help you to share documents – so a good tip may be to not put anything too private, like passwords, on there. One errant click may send it to the wrong person.

Finally, cookies are designed to improve your browsing experience by tracking and saving information about your visits to a site, helping to personalise your sessions. Deleting your browsing history may help, but there are certain apps which can block them if you don’t feel comfortable.

So, if you want to maintain your privacy online, maybe only share things you’d be happy with a stranger seeing – and if you don’t feel comfortable with cookies, you might decide to invest in some tech to block them. If that’s not enough, just don’t accept them and visit another site – and why not have a yummy cookie to eat instead?

vocabulary.entry: private /ˈpraɪvət/ adj. 私密的；私人的
vocabulary.example: She values her private life and rarely talks about it in public.
vocabulary.translation: 她很珍视自己的私人生活，很少在公开场合提及。

vocabulary.entry: relationship status /rɪˈleɪʃnʃɪp ˈsteɪtəs/ n. 感情状况
vocabulary.example: He didn't want to disclose his relationship status on the form.
vocabulary.translation: 他不想在表格上透露自己的感情状况。

vocabulary.entry: digital footprint /ˈdɪdʒɪtl ˈfʊtprɪnt/ n. 数字足迹
vocabulary.example: Your digital footprint includes all the data you leave online.
vocabulary.translation: 你的数字足迹包括你在网络上留下的所有数据。

vocabulary.entry: display /dɪˈspleɪ/ v. 展示；发布
vocabulary.example: The museum displays a collection of ancient artifacts.
vocabulary.translation: 这家博物馆展出了一批古代文物藏品。

vocabulary.entry: connection /kəˈnekʃn/ n. 社交关系；人脉
vocabulary.example: She used her business connections to get the job.
vocabulary.translation: 她利用自己的商业人脉得到了这份工作。

vocabulary.entry: holiday snap /ˈhɒlədeɪ snæp/ n. 度假快照
vocabulary.example: She posted some holiday snaps on her Instagram account.
vocabulary.translation: 她在自己的照片墙账号上发了几张度假快照。

vocabulary.entry: random /ˈrændəm/ adj. 随机的；陌生的
vocabulary.example: A random stranger offered to help me carry the heavy bags.
vocabulary.translation: 一个陌生路人主动帮我提沉重的袋子。

vocabulary.entry: cookie /ˈkʊki/ n. 网站跟踪数据（计算机术语）
vocabulary.example: This website uses cookies to improve your browsing experience.
vocabulary.translation: 该网站使用Cookie来优化你的浏览体验。

vocabulary.entry: pop up /pɒp ʌp/ v. 突然出现；弹出
vocabulary.example: A warning message popped up on the screen.
vocabulary.translation: 屏幕上突然弹出了一条警告信息。

vocabulary.entry: privacy setting /ˈprɪvəsi ˈsetɪŋ/ n. 隐私设置
vocabulary.example: You should adjust your privacy setting to protect your personal data.
vocabulary.translation: 你应该调整隐私设置来保护个人数据。

vocabulary.entry: platform /ˈplætfɔːm/ n. 平台
vocabulary.example: This is a popular platform for online learning.
vocabulary.translation: 这是一个很受欢迎的在线学习平台。

vocabulary.entry: by default /baɪ dɪˈfɔːlt/ 处于默认状态
vocabulary.example: The software is set to save files in this format by default.
vocabulary.translation: 这款软件默认将文件保存为这种格式。

vocabulary.entry: onus /ˈəʊnəs/ n. 责任；义务
vocabulary.example: The onus is on the employer to provide a safe working environment.
vocabulary.translation: 雇主有责任提供安全的工作环境。

vocabulary.entry: boundary /ˈbaʊndri/ n. 边界；界限
vocabulary.example: It's important to set clear boundaries between work and life.
vocabulary.translation: 在工作和生活之间设定清晰的界限很重要。

vocabulary.entry: confine /kənˈfaɪn/ v. 限制；局限于
vocabulary.example: The problem is not confined to this region alone.
vocabulary.translation: 这个问题并不仅限于该地区。

vocabulary.entry: document /ˈdɒkjumənt/ n. 文件；文档
vocabulary.example: Please read through this document before signing it.
vocabulary.translation: 请在签署前通读这份文件。

vocabulary.entry: password /ˈpɑːswɜːd/ n. 密码
vocabulary.example: Make sure you choose a strong password for your email account.
vocabulary.translation: 一定要为你的邮箱账号设置一个安全系数高的密码。

vocabulary.entry: errant /ˈerənt/ adj. 错误的；偏离正轨的
vocabulary.example: An errant click on the link took her to a wrong website.
vocabulary.translation: 一次误点链接让她进入了错误的网站。

vocabulary.entry: track /træk/ v. 追踪；跟踪
vocabulary.example: The app can track your daily steps and calorie consumption.
vocabulary.translation: 这款应用可以追踪你的每日步数和卡路里消耗。

vocabulary.entry: personalise /ˈpɜːsənəlaɪz/ v. 使个性化；量身定制
vocabulary.example: You can personalise the homepage according to your preferences.
vocabulary.translation: 你可以根据自己的喜好个性化设置主页。

vocabulary.entry: browsing history /ˈbraʊzɪŋ ˈhɪstri/ n. 浏览历史
vocabulary.example: He deleted his browsing history to protect his privacy.
vocabulary.translation: 他删除了浏览历史以保护自己的隐私。

vocabulary.entry: block /blɒk/ v. 拦截；阻止
vocabulary.example: This software can block unwanted ads and pop-ups.
vocabulary.translation: 这款软件可以拦截不想要的广告和弹窗。

vocabulary.entry: maintain /meɪnˈteɪn/ v. 维持；保持
vocabulary.example: It's difficult to maintain privacy in the digital age.
vocabulary.translation: 在数字时代，保护隐私并非易事。

vocabulary.entry: invest in /ɪnˈvest ɪn/ 投入（时间、金钱等）；购置
vocabulary.example: She decided to invest in a good antivirus software.
vocabulary.translation: 她决定买一款优质的杀毒软件。

vocabulary.entry: yummy /ˈjʌmi/ adj. 美味的；可口的
vocabulary.example: These chocolate cookies are really yummy.
vocabulary.translation: 这些巧克力曲奇饼真的很好吃。

sentences.english: Some of us like to keep some things private – maybe we don’t want people knowing about our relationship status, our age or where we live – because these details are personal.
sentences.chinese: 我们中有些人总喜欢保留一些隐私——可能不愿让别人知道自己的感情状况、年龄或是住址，因为这些都属于个人私密信息。

sentences.english: The problem is, everywhere we go online, we seem to leave a digital footprint.
sentences.chinese: 但问题在于，我们在网络上的每一次足迹，似乎都会留下数字痕迹。

sentences.english: On our social media accounts, we often display things like our opinions, connections and holiday snaps.
sentences.chinese: 我们常常会在社交媒体账号上分享自己的观点、社交关系和度假照片。

sentences.english: The issue is, how do we stop everybody seeing everything?
sentences.chinese: 但问题是，如何才能避免自己的所有信息被所有人看到呢？

sentences.english: Maybe we don’t want a random stranger knowing our favourite type of coffee.
sentences.chinese: 或许我们并不想让陌生路人知道自己爱喝哪种咖啡。

sentences.english: And cookies – there was a time they were just something nice to eat. Now they seem to be popping up on websites.
sentences.chinese: 还有“Cookie”——曾几何时，这个词还只指代美味的甜点，如今却频频出现在各类网站中。

sentences.english: So how can you stay more private?
sentences.chinese: 那么，怎样才能更好地保护自己的网络隐私呢？

sentences.english: There are some steps you can take.
sentences.chinese: 其实我们可以采取一些措施。

sentences.english: First, on your social media accounts, check your privacy settings.
sentences.chinese: 首先，查看自己社交媒体账号的隐私设置。

sentences.english: Many social media platforms allow everything to be visible by default, and the onus is on you to set your boundaries.
sentences.chinese: 许多社交平台默认将所有内容设为公开可见，因此设置信息分享边界的责任需要由你自己承担。

sentences.english: And limiting the amount you share isn’t only confined to social media.
sentences.chinese: 而且限制分享内容这件事，并不仅限于社交媒体。

sentences.english: There are many sites out there that help you to share documents – so a good tip may be to not put anything too private, like passwords, on there.
sentences.chinese: 有很多网站都提供文件分享功能，一个实用的小建议是，不要在这些平台上传过于私密的内容，比如密码之类的信息。

sentences.english: One errant click may send it to the wrong person.
sentences.chinese: 一个误操作的点击，就可能把信息发给错误的对象。

sentences.english: Finally, cookies are designed to improve your browsing experience by tracking and saving information about your visits to a site, helping to personalise your sessions.
sentences.chinese: 最后需要说明的是，网站Cookie的设计初衷，是通过追踪并保存用户的网站访问记录，来优化浏览体验，实现个性化的访问服务。

sentences.english: Deleting your browsing history may help, but there are certain apps which can block them if you don’t feel comfortable.
sentences.chinese: 删除浏览记录或许能起到一定作用，但如果你对此仍有顾虑，也可以借助一些专门的应用程序来拦截Cookie。

sentences.english: So, if you want to maintain your privacy online, maybe only share things you’d be happy with a stranger seeing – and if you don’t feel comfortable with cookies, you might decide to invest in some tech to block them.
sentences.chinese: 所以，如果你想保护自己的网络隐私，不妨只分享那些即便是陌生人看到也无妨的内容。而如果对网站Cookie心存芥蒂，你可以考虑借助相关技术工具来拦截它们。

sentences.english: If that’s not enough, just don’t accept them and visit another site – and why not have a yummy cookie to eat instead?
sentences.chinese: 要是这些方法还不够，那就直接拒绝Cookie，换一个网站访问吧——与此同时，何不享用一块美味的曲奇饼干呢？
